File: docs/BENCHMARKS_AB_CASE_STUDY.md 1 | # 📄 Empirical Evaluation of Hybrid Multi-Tier AI Routing in Autonomous Coding Agents 2 | ## A Comparative A/B Case Study on Cost Optimization, Quality Preservation, and Reasoning Fidelity 3 | 4 | **Author:** [@dixieflatline76](https://github.com/dixieflatline76) · [spicebox.dev/nacho-flow](https://spicebox.dev/nacho-flow/) 5 | **Date:** August 2026 6 | **Document Classification:** Technical Whitepaper & Empirical Benchmark Report 7 | **Document Version:** `1.0.0` (Official Release, Aligned with Nacho Flow `v0.6.0`) 8 | 9 | --- 10 | 11 | ## 🔬 Executive Summary 12 | 13 | Autonomous AI coding agents (such as **Roo Code**, **Cline**, **Cursor**, and **Aider**) operate via iterative feedback loops where accumulated conversational history, project file maps, terminal outputs, and diagnostics are re-transmitted on every single turn. This architectural pattern induces a severe **"Context Snowball"**, causing routine turn costs (e.g., inspecting a log, checking a syntax definition, or executing `git status`) to cost upwards of $2.00–$3.00 per prompt at frontier cloud rates. 14 | 15 | This whitepaper presents an empirical, head-to-head A/B case study evaluating **Nacho Flow**—a high-performance, deterministic semantic AI gateway built in pure Go.
